description: SANS/CWE Top 25 Most Dangerous Software Errors mapped to GitHub security settings

rules.name: Secret scanning prevents hardcoded credentials (CWE-798)
rules.description: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials. Secret scanning must be enabled to detect hardcoded credentials, API keys, tokens, and passwords committed to the repository.
rules.remediation: Enable secret scanning in Repository Settings > Code security and analysis to detect hardcoded credentials.

rules.name: Push protection blocks credential commits (CWE-798)
rules.description: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials. Push protection must be enabled to block commits containing detected secrets before they reach the repository.
rules.remediation: Enable push protection in Repository Settings > Code security and analysis > Push protection.

rules.name: No open secret scanning alerts (CWE-798)
rules.description: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials. All secret scanning alerts must be resolved and exposed credentials rotated to prevent exploitation of leaked secrets.
rules.remediation: Rotate all exposed credentials immediately. Resolve all open secret scanning alerts in the Security tab.

rules.name: Branch protection enforces access control (CWE-284)
rules.description: CWE-284: Improper Access Control. Branch protection rules must be enabled on the default branch to enforce proper access controls and prevent unauthorized modifications.
rules.remediation: Enable branch protection rules on the default branch to enforce access control policies.

rules.name: Default org permission restricts access (CWE-284)
rules.description: CWE-284: Improper Access Control. Organization default repository permissions should be 'none' or 'read' to enforce the principle of least privilege.
rules.remediation: Set default repository permission to 'No permission' or 'Read' in Organization Settings > Member privileges.

rules.name: Pull request reviews enforce access control (CWE-284)
rules.description: CWE-284: Improper Access Control. Required pull request reviews ensure that code changes are reviewed by authorized personnel before being merged.
rules.remediation: Require at least one approving review before merging in branch protection settings.

rules.name: Admin privileges properly scoped (CWE-269)
rules.description: CWE-269: Improper Privilege Management. Repository admin permissions should be limited, and CODEOWNERS should be configured to ensure changes to critical files require appropriate approval.
rules.remediation: Create a CODEOWNERS file to define code ownership and required reviewers for critical paths.

rules.name: Force push disabled prevents privilege abuse (CWE-269)
rules.description: CWE-269: Improper Privilege Management. Force pushes should be disabled on protected branches to prevent privileged users from rewriting history to hide unauthorized changes.
rules.remediation: Disable force pushes in branch protection settings to prevent history manipulation.

rules.name: Member repository creation restricted (CWE-269)
rules.description: CWE-269: Improper Privilege Management. Regular organization members should not be able to create repositories without oversight to prevent uncontrolled resource proliferation.
rules.remediation: Restrict repository creation to organization owners in Organization Settings > Member privileges.

rules.name: Signed commits ensure data integrity (CWE-311)
rules.description: CWE-311: Missing Encryption of Sensitive Data. Signed commits should be required to ensure the authenticity and integrity of code changes through cryptographic verification.
rules.remediation: Require signed commits in branch protection settings to verify commit authenticity.

rules.name: Private repository for sensitive content (CWE-311)
rules.description: CWE-311: Missing Encryption of Sensitive Data. Repositories containing sensitive data or internal infrastructure code should be private or internal, not public.
rules.remediation: Change repository visibility to private or internal if it contains sensitive content.

rules.name: Workflow artifacts handled securely (CWE-502)
rules.description: CWE-502: Deserialization of Untrusted Data. Workflow permissions should be restricted to prevent untrusted artifacts from being processed with elevated privileges.
rules.remediation: Set default workflow permissions to read-only. Use explicit permission grants in workflow files.

rules.name: Fork PR workflows require approval (CWE-502)
rules.description: CWE-502: Deserialization of Untrusted Data. Fork pull request workflows must require approval to prevent processing of untrusted data from malicious forks.
rules.remediation: Require approval for fork pull request workflows in Repository Settings > Actions > General.

rules.name: Actions restricted to trusted sources (CWE-829)
rules.description: CWE-829: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere. GitHub Actions should be restricted to selected trusted actions to prevent inclusion of untrusted third-party functionality.
rules.remediation: Restrict allowed actions to verified creators and pin actions to specific SHA hashes.

rules.name: Status checks validate third-party integrations (CWE-829)
rules.description: CWE-829: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere. Required status checks should be configured to validate that third-party integrations are functioning correctly before merge.
rules.remediation: Configure required status checks in branch protection to validate all integrations before merge.

rules.name: Organization app installations governed (CWE-829)
rules.description: CWE-829: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere. Installed GitHub Apps should be reviewed and limited to trusted, necessary applications only.
rules.remediation: Review all installed GitHub Apps in Organization Settings > Third-party access. Remove unnecessary apps.
